document.title: Pre-Technical Conferences Comments of ENGIE North America Inc. re the PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reforms
document.group: PJM governance and stakeholder reform vote

pages.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
 
) 
PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reforms   ) 
 
 
Docket No. AD26-7-000 
   
 
) 
 
 
  
 
PRE-TECHNICAL CONFERENCES COMMENTS OF  
ENGIE NORTH AMERICA, INC.  
 
(July 22, 2026) 
 
ENGIE North America, Inc.1 (“ENGIE”) commends the Federal Energy Regulatory 
Commission’s (“FERC”) leadership for convening this technical conference to explore the 
fundamental issues and key policy considerations necessary to ensure the long-term success of 
the PJM Interconnection (“PJM”). We respectfully submit these comments and look forward to 
following the discussion on July 23 and to future engagement with the Commission and 
stakeholders.  
ENGIE encourages reforms that strengthen confidence in PJM’s governance and stakeholder 
processes while preserving the critical role that PJM’s competitive wholesale markets play in 
maintaining reliability, supporting investment, and promoting affordability across the region.  
More specifically, we propose reforms that: 
• Reaffirm the criticality of the PJM wholesale markets to regional reliability, economic 
investment and affordability in the PJM footprint; 
 
• Refocus the PJM Board role on governance;  
 
• Allow for a framework for state executive-level electricity policy discussions outside of 
the PJM stakeholder process, such as the New England States Committee on Electricity 
(“NESCOE”), to enhance states’ interactions with PJM, Board and stakeholders; and  
 
1 ENGIE North America (“ENGIE”) is a subsidiary of ENGIE SA, a global energy company and one of the world’s largest 
producers of energy.  With roots that trace back 180 years, we own and operate 110 GW of power generation, including 46 GW 
of natural gas generation, 6 GW of nuclear generation, and 57 GW of renewable generation – with 11 GW in North America. 
ENGIE operates the largest natural gas distribution network in Europe, owns 2,485 miles of transmission lines, is a global leading 
energy supplier to commercial and industrial customers, and is a significant supplier of U.S. produced LNG to Europe.

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 2 
 
2 
 
 
• Accelerate the stakeholder decision-making process and enhance meaningful stakeholder 
input through both procedural and substantive changes.  
 
I. 
COMMENTS 
 
a. PJM markets are critical to regional reliability, economic investment, and 
affordability in the PJM footprint. 
 
PJM has brought significant value to customers in the region during its 30 years as a 
regional transmission organization (“RTO”), including improved reliability, lower system costs, 
more efficient transmission planning, and improved investor certainty.  
Consequently, the prospect of PJM’s disaggregation is counterproductive. If ‘speed to 
power’ is the principal regional and national priority, then disassembling PJM in favor of a yet –
to-be determined framework through an undefined transition design and timeline will not satisfy 
that objective. The foundation of PJM is sound, but some reforms may be needed to regain 
stakeholder confidence and ensure market competitiveness, while providing consumers with 
affordable energy. 
b. Proposed Reforms on Governance 
 
1. The PJM Board should focus on governance. 
 
Stakeholders advise; PJM manages; and the Board governs. These principles of an 
independent board include objective oversight, uncompromised integrity, and the protection of 
long-term stakeholder value. ENGIE supports a Board independent from outside and special 
interests, and that is responsive and willing to engage with regional stakeholders on topics of 
strategic importance.  
The PJM Board should focus on the traditional and essential matters of governance: 
providing strategic oversight, ensuring accountability, managing risk, and promoting PJM’s 
long-term success. The Board should not be excessively involved in the tactical stakeholder

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 3 
 
3 
 
process. It is an inefficient use of time and resources for the Board to participate directly in 
stakeholder decision-making exercises, such as evaluating a matrix of many complex and 
competing choices. The Board should instead be advised of and consulted on major reforms so 
that Board members are appropriately informed, remain accountable and, in turn, can hold the 
PJM organization responsible for implementation of market design and other changes.  
Because implementing this change will necessarily require both increased interaction 
between PJM leadership and the Board and decreased direct Board interaction with stakeholders,   
in the inevitable transition period, it is important that regional stakeholders are reassured that the 
Board will continue to keep stakeholder interests in mind in the long term. PJM stakeholders 
should have regular, formal and informal opportunities to meet with the Board to discuss items 
of interest. For example, market participants in New England meet with the ISO-NE Board twice 
a year in meetings with their New England Power Pool (“NEPOOL”) sectors. The Board also 
engages through other regional opportunities such as with the ISO-NE Consumer Liaison Group 
and the New England Conference of Public Utilities Commissioners and are generally responsive 
to individual market participant outreach.  
Refocusing the PJM Board on strategic governance matters will affect the role of senior 
leadership, which will be required to take a more singular role in managing stakeholder relations 
and making final decisions on market reforms. With PJM leadership taking on a more decisive 
role in final decision-making PJM leadership must be increasingly available to stakeholders both 
within and outside of the stakeholder process to demonstrate their understanding and 
commitment to stakeholder requests and inquiries.

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 4 
 
4 
 
2. Improve states’ ability to engage with PJM and stakeholders 
through an independent framework for executive-level electricity 
policy discussions.  
 
ENGIE supports a robust, collaborative, and communicative relationship between the 
PJM member states, the PJM Board and PJM leadership and market participants. States are 
important customers and policymakers, and their decisions can have significant consequences on 
the wholesale markets. We offer some observations based on our experience in PJM and other 
regions.  
Generally, in regions where there are mediating institutions outside of the RTO/ISO 
stakeholder process that facilitate state collaboration on electricity issues states have an enhanced 
opportunity to communicate and collaborate before engaging with the ISO/RTO and market 
participants. States can discuss differences, identify areas of common interest, and where 
possible develop consensus positions before engaging with ISO/RTO leadership, the Board, and 
stakeholders.  
While the Organization of PJM States (“OPSI”) provides one arena for states to 
communicate concerns, ENGIE recommends further developing a consensus-driven framework 
for executive level state engagement outside of the PJM stakeholder process. States should 
consider forming a new organization that represents the PJM governors on electricity issues to 
facilitate state executive level collaboration. The template we have in mind is NESCOE, who 
represents the collective perspective of the six New England governors on regional electricity 
matters. NESCOE is effective in the NEPOOL stakeholder process, and with ISO-NE and the 
ISO-NE Board and works in collaboration with the New England Conference of Public Utilities 
Commissioners (“NECPUC”).

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 5 
 
5 
 
Such an organization would be instrumental in facilitating collaborative discussions 
between the states and PJM leadership and the PJM Board. It could allow PJM leadership to 
engage regularly with the governors and their representatives on major market reforms, increase 
engagement on reliability assessments and planning assumptions, allow formal opportunities for 
state input before major tariff filings, and convene regular meetings with the PJM Board. The 
PJM Board should, likewise, consider assigning individual Board members to interact with states 
to increase communication between the Board and the states, as is done in New England.  
Instituting an independent framework for better organizing and representing governors in 
the PJM footprint, even when they disagree over policy, will permit the governors to better 
represent their views before the PJM Board, PJM leadership and with market participants. 
Further, increased early collaboration amongst governors and PJM leadership and the Board 
should help to streamline the governors’ role in the stakeholder process and reduce friction.  In 
turn, this would help streamline the overall PJM decision-making process.  
c. Proposed Stakeholder Process Reforms 
 
ENGIE believes that the existing stakeholder process has served PJM well for many 
years by promoting broad stakeholder participation and some level of transparency. The primary 
challenge today is ensuring the process can reach timely decisions. While some practices were 
intended to address critical issues quickly, the pace, scale, and uncertainty of load growth in the 
region today has thwarted those practices and they may now prolong deliberation and delay the 
resolution of critical market design issues.  
Consequently, a swift, thorough and inclusive stakeholder process in PJM is more critical 
than ever. Durable solutions to the region’s resource adequacy challenges will require enhanced

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 6 
 
6 
 
collaboration, open dialogue, and a shared understanding among PJM, market participants, and 
the states.  
None of our proposed changes should be construed to undermine the importance of 
market participants to the PJM markets and stakeholder process.  Market participants’ 
commercial and operational experience is critical to adequately evaluate proposed market design 
reforms. Without the benefit of market participant experience, PJM reforms risk being practically 
or commercially infeasible or having adverse unintended consequences.  
States are also critical stakeholders and should have a voice in the stakeholder process. 
However, PJM’s markets must remain operationally independent and regionally focused. State 
policies affect the resource mix, transmission development, electrification, and load growth, and 
therefore should be communicated and considered during market design efforts. Building a voice 
for the states includes more meaningful and earlier opportunities to shape discussions, 
particularly where state policies affect resource development. 
Finally, ENGIE believes PJM staff have done a masterful job of facilitating collaboration 
and identifying differences across the diverse stakeholder interests. What ENGIE recommends 
for faster decision-making is a mandate from FERC, the Board, and stakeholders to allow PJM 
senior leadership to act more decisively in proposing final decisions on market reforms. 
i. 
Accelerate stakeholder decision-making through greater discipline and focus 
during the stakeholder process. 
 
The stakeholder process can be accelerated through greater discipline and focus at every 
level of the governance structure. As issues move from working groups to subcommittees, 
committees, and ultimately the Board, participants are often required to revisit the same 
discussions, presentations, and questions multiple times. While stakeholder engagement is 
essential, excessive repetition can slow decision-making, consume significant resources, and

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 7 
 
7 
 
delay outcomes on matters that are increasingly urgent for the region. A more disciplined 
approach should ensure that each level of the stakeholder process builds upon prior work rather 
than revisiting issues that have already been evaluated.  
PJM should also adopt stronger meeting management practices to ensure discussions 
remain productive and focused. Effective facilitation, coupled with active time management 
during presentations and Q&A, can help curb repetitive or off-topic comments and keep 
proceedings moving forward. Implementing clear time limits for presentations, questions, and 
stakeholder comments would encourage concise, substantive participation while ensuring all 
perspectives are heard. These measures would improve the efficiency of the stakeholder process 
without diminishing transparency or inclusiveness. 
ii. 
Accelerate stakeholder consideration of PJM proposals through greater 
transparency in analytical assumptions and decision rationale.  
 
Data.  Data.  Data.  ENGIE believes that a core responsibility of an ISO/RTO is to 
provide data, analysis methodology, and assumptions to market participants so they can reach 
their own conclusions and make commercial decisions accordingly. In general, surprises lead to 
confusion, consternation at times, and detract from efficient and timely discovery and resolution 
of needed market reforms.  
Greater transparency in both analytical assumptions made by PJM in its proposals as well 
as in its decision rationale when choosing to move forward with proposals would significantly 
improve stakeholder understanding of the proposals and at the same time build credibility and 
garner trust. Earlier publication of modeling inputs, more detailed documentation of sensitivity 
analyses, better visibility into reliability and market benefit calculations, and discussion and 
documentation of tradeoffs considered by PJM staff and explanations of why PJM supports or 
opposes stakeholder proposals are essential to an improved stakeholder process. Stakeholders

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 8 
 
8 
 
may disagree on outcomes, but confidence increases when everyone understands the data, 
assumptions, and rational underlying a decision.  
ENGIE is particularly concerned with the lack of information and rigor in the stakeholder 
process when designing new market products. At times market participants have been assured 
that new market products will not significantly alter market pricing but the products have instead 
led to significant price volatility. More upfront information and increased transparency in 
analysis would improve market participants’ awareness and permit them to hedge risks 
appropriately.   
Generally, process reforms should focus on ensuring robust stakeholder input, improving 
transparency of PJM proposals and transparency into decision-making rationale, combined with 
the ability to make timely decisions that support reliability and efficient investment. We 
recommend the Commission consider the following reforms to PJM’s stakeholder process: 
• Replace affiliate voting at lower levels with a ‘one company, one vote’ structure 
so that no one stakeholder has an outsized influence on the vote outcome; 
 
• Publish votes of all committees to promote transparency and accountability in 
stakeholder voting;  
 
• Increase transparency of PJM proposals specifically in analytical assumptions 
which would improve stakeholder understanding of PJM proposals and increase 
credibility and trust. PJM should focus on earlier publication of modeling inputs, 
more detailed documentation of sensitivity analyses, and better visibility into 
reliability and market benefit calculations.  
 
• Increase transparency in PJM staff and PJM leadership decision rationale through 
more in-depth discussions and documentation of tradeoffs considered by PJM 
staff and explanations of why PJM supports or opposes stakeholder proposals, 
especially when PJM leadership selects one avenue when stakeholder views are 
divided.  
 
• Encourage the states to create a framework for governors to collaborate 
meaningfully in the stakeholder process through an outside organization, such as 
NESCOE. PJM should engage regularly with the governors and focus on early

ENGIE Comments  
Docket No. AD26-07-000 
Page 9 
 
9 
 
consultation, education and opportunities to review significant rule amendments 
and/or other major undertakings. 
 
A thoughtfully reformed stakeholder process that incorporates these changes would build 
on many of PJM’s strengths and improve decision-making efficiency, strengthen stakeholder 
confidence, and enhance PJM’s ability to address pressing challenges while preserving 
meaningful opportunities for stakeholder engagement and consensus-building.  
II. 
CONCLUSION 
ENGIE respectfully requests that the Commission consider these recommendations as it 
evaluates opportunities to strengthen PJM’s governance and stakeholder processes. The proposed 
reforms would improve decision-making, enhance transparency and accountability, restore 
stakeholder confidence, and better position PJM to address the reliability, affordability, and 
investment challenges facing the region without requiring disruptive structural changes to the 
existing PJM markets. 
 
Respectfully submitted,
